_note: vCAOC standing rules of engagement for DCS World campaigns: the part of every campaign's ROE that does not change. Each campaign adds its declared hostile forces, default weapons control status, measures (on/off), ID and commit criteria, weapons restrictions, restricted targets and remarks; the theater adds its own rules. Game use only, not for real-world operations.

general.title: Law of armed conflict
general.text: All forces comply with the law of armed conflict: military necessity, distinction, proportionality and the avoidance of unnecessary suffering.

general.title: Self-defense
general.text: Nothing in these ROE limits the inherent right and obligation of self-defense. Aircrew may take all necessary and proportional action in response to an attack or the threat of an imminent attack on friendly forces, without further authority.

general.title: Precedence
general.text: These ROE take precedence over unit SOPs. The SPINS set out how they are applied; where the SPINS and the ROE differ, the ROE govern.

surface.title: Positive identification
surface.text: Positive identification (PID) of every target is required before engagement: reasonable certainty that the object of attack is a valid target under these ROE.

surface.title: Protected structures
surface.text: Hospitals, schools, religious and cultural sites, civilian population centers, and facilities marked with the Red Cross or Red Crescent are protected and are never targeted.

surface.title: Planned targets
surface.text: Targets tasked on the ATO have been cleared by the JFACC for PID and collateral damage. Aircrew do not move the aimpoint, move to a heavier weapon class or shorten the fuze delay without JFACC approval.

surface.title: Dynamic targets
surface.text: Targets found during the mission are reported to the controlling agency and cleared before attack, unless a time-sensitive or troops-in-contact authority below applies.

surface.title: Time-sensitive targets
surface.text: When there is no time to obtain JFACC approval, the mission commander may authorize precision fires on enemy leadership, MANPADS, artillery and rocket systems, and UAV launch systems.

surface.title: Troops in contact
surface.text: The on-scene commander of friendly forces in contact may authorize fires against positively identified declared hostile forces, deconflicting from protected structures and restricted targets.

surface.title: Collateral damage
surface.text: Aircrew assess collateral damage before every attack. Where harm to civilians or civilian objects is likely, the attack needs controlling-agency approval; where it is high, JFACC approval.

idTerms: A contact identified as enemy upon which clearance to fire is authorized under these ROE.
A contact identified as enemy by the ID criteria. Does not by itself authorize engagement.
A contact whose identity is unknown.
A contact identified as a friendly aircraft, ship or ground position.
A contact identified as belonging to neither side. Never engaged.
A contact with friendly IFF/SIF but no other friendly indication; treated as a BOGEY until identified.
A BOGEY complying with the ACO or safe-passage procedures.
A contact that meets the point-of-origin criteria in the ID criteria.
declareNote: The hostile act and hostile intent criteria below are used to declare a contact HOSTILE. A HOSTILE declaration authorizes engagement under these ROE, before any attack is imminent; it is separate from, and adds to, the right of self-defense in 1.2.
hostileAct: A weapons launch, or any other attack or use of force against friendly forces.
hostileIntent: A correlated fire-control radar lock (spike) on friendly forces.
Clearly and persistently manoeuvring into a weapons-launch position against friendly forces.
High-speed, hot-aspect approach toward friendly forces or high-value airborne assets.
Dispensing countermeasures or jamming while closing on friendly forces.
enemyIndications: A clear non-cooperative target recognition (NCTR) reply.
A passive electronic support measures (ESM) correlation.
Visual identification, including with a targeting pod.
Groups splitting from a BANDIT or HOSTILE group keep that identification.
wcs: Fire at any target positively identified as BANDIT or HOSTILE.
Fire only at targets identified as HOSTILE.
Fire only in self-defense or in response to a formal order.

air.title: Commit authority
air.text: Commit authority rests with the controlling agency ({awacs}). Fighters may recommend a commit.

air.title: Formal order
air.text: A formal order is given as "SHOOT GROUP (name)" with the JFACC authentication.

declaredHostileDefault: All RED coalition military forces, their aircraft, vehicles, ships, weapons and supporting structures in the AO.

measures.text: HOSTILE is declared by the AWACS ({awacs}). With no AWACS contact, flight leads may declare using the ID criteria.
Beyond-visual-range engagement is authorized against contacts declared HOSTILE.
Visual identification is required before any air-to-air engagement.
Pursuit of HOSTILE aircraft beyond the FLOT is authorized.
Civil and neutral aircraft are not engaged; report them to the AWACS.
Short of the FSCL, release only under JTAC or FAC(A) control.
Weapons free on ground targets inside open killboxes, within the killbox altitude block.
SEAD and DEAD flights may engage any emitting enemy SAM radar without further clearance.
Time-sensitive targets need CAOC approval before attack (the mission commander's TST authority is withdrawn).
Graduated force: a show of presence, then a show of force, before lethal action against threats showing hostile intent.
Hung ordnance is jettisoned only in the jettison areas published in the SPINS.

rules: On the NTTR, weapons employment only on scheduled ranges and inside each range's boundaries and altitude blocks.
No live or simulated releases outside the ranges; jettison only in designated areas.
